title: na4h: whitelist check in run_session with IPv4-mapped normalization
description:
## What
Implement the actual whitelist check inside run_session. Normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses before checking. Set connection_whitelisted local variable for use by future greylisting code.

## Algorithm
1. In session.rs, after client_ip is extracted (currently lines 171-174), add normalization:
   ```rust
   let client_ip = match client_ip {
       IpAddr::V6(v6) => v6.to_ipv4_mapped()
           .map(IpAddr::V4)
           .unwrap_or(IpAddr::V6(v6)),
       v4 => v4,
   };
   ```
   Note: use to_ipv4_mapped() (not to_ipv4()) — the former only matches the ::ffff:0:0/96 range (true IPv4-mapped), the latter also matches deprecated ::0:0/96 IPv4-compatible addresses. to_ipv4_mapped() is correct.

2. Immediately after normalization, compute:
   ```rust
   let connection_whitelisted = config.peer_whitelist.iter()
       .any(|net| net.contains(&client_ip));
   ```

3. Add a tracing log line:
   ```rust
   if connection_whitelisted {
       info!(peer = %peer_addr, "connection whitelisted — spam filters bypassed");
   }
   ```

4. The connection_whitelisted variable is now available throughout run_session for future use by greylisting (mgzn epic). Leave a comment: `// used by greylisting (stoa-ef702cf6) to bypass RCPT TO delay`

5. For now, the variable is not yet consumed (no DNSBL/FCrDNS/greylist to bypass yet) — the compiler will warn about unused variable. Suppress with `let _ = connection_whitelisted;` OR prefix with `#[allow(unused_variables)]` if clippy objects. Prefer `let _connection_whitelisted = ...` to preserve the name for future use.

## Defensive rules
- Use to_ipv4_mapped(), NOT to_ipv4() — see algorithm note
- The check must come AFTER normalization, not before
- No unwrap() on the normalization path — the match handles all cases
- connection_whitelisted must never be used to skip AUTH — authentication is always required regardless of whitelist status. Add a comment to this effect.

## Tests
Written in na4h.3 — this bead just implements.
